decision.notes: a fraud caught saves the ride's fare; a review costs 25,000 (a tenth of a typical fare); the team reviews at most 0.5% of the rides

gate.chosen: the decision is chosen on every seed (an operating point with a share, none when no review pays; no refusal)
gate.capacity: on every seed that acted, the holdout's actions never exceed the capacity share of its rows (with one row's rounding)
gate.coverage: among the seeds that chose to act (at least 20), the realised value per ride lies inside the choice's 90% prediction interval on at least 80% of them
gate.centre: each seed's z = (realised - the interval's centre) / (its half-width / 1.645); |mean z| <= 1.645 / sqrt(N)
gate.width: the 90% chi-squared interval of the root mean square of z contains 1 (neither too narrow nor too wide)
gate.inconclusive: fewer than 20 seeds acting: no verdict on the interval
gate.next: a pass: keep the 0.114.0 interval; too narrow with misses on both sides: compare each fold model's holdout value with the final model's before changing the interval again; too wide: drop the one-fold samples; centre below 0: correct the optimism of choosing the model

objective: Does the decision core keep its word through the engine on the delivery-fraud replica? A stated review decision, chosen on out-of-fold scores, against what it realises on the holdout read once, over thirty fresh seeds: how often it lands inside its interval, and how far off and to which side it misses (dclab-core 0.114.0's interval).
